overview.oneLineTake: Direct US-Iran conflict, record energy prices, and a hawkish Fed reprice are pushing markets into a stagflationary risk-off regime with expanding volatility across equities and rates.
themes: Direct US-Iran military escalation and Hormuz Strait supply threats are driving oil/diesel to record highs, repricing the inflation outlook
Strong August payrolls (+162k) triggered a hawkish Fed reprice, lifting yields toward 4.8% and pressuring equities
China is injecting $54bn+ into banks/insurers to combat property weakness while halting rare earth shipments to the US
AI/memory chip trade remains a crowded bright spot (Micron, Sandisk, Korean semis) even as broad markets weaken
Commodity inflation is broadening: copper at all-time highs, food prices at 2022 peaks, and iron ore reclaiming $100
risks: Strait of Hormuz closure or Iranian "restricted zone" could trigger an immediate oil spike and global supply shock
Stagflationary dynamics are building: manufacturing/construction data is softening while energy and food costs accelerate
Japan sold a record $80bn of reserves (likely Treasuries) to defend the yen, adding Treasury supply pressure
Credit stress signals are emerging (Australian developer insolvency, FICO plunge, complex debt concerns)
